jobs.jd: At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries. Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities. Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem. Role Overview The Business Intelligence (BI) Solution Developer serves as a key member of the Measurement Enablement team, responsible for ensuring client healthcare marketing data is accurate, current, and ready for reporting and analysis. This role bridges the gap between Data Engineering, analytics teams, and client stakeholders by managing data ingestion processes, validating data quality, maintaining reporting-ready data structures, and resolving issues throughout the data lifecycle. The ideal candidate enjoys investigating data questions, identifying root causes of data discrepancies, improving data quality, and working across multiple teams to ensure reliable data powers business decisions. This role can be remote within the United States or based in any of our U.S. office locations, including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Lambertville, NJ, San Francisco, or Carmel, IN. Primary Responsibilities Data Ingestion & Source Management Coordinate the onboarding of new client data sources and data feeds. Partner with Data Engineering to ensure successful ingestion of data into Databricks. Monitor data delivery schedules and ingestion processes. Maintain source documentation, field mappings, and data inventories. Work directly with internal teams and external partners to resolve source-related issues. Data Quality & Stewardship Monitor data freshness, completeness, and accuracy across client datasets. Perform ongoing quality assurance and reconciliation checks. Investigate missing, unexpected, or inconsistent data. Escalate, coordinate and resolve remediation efforts with the appropriate teams. Maintain documentation of data quality findings and resolutions. Support the development of automated data quality checks and monitoring processes. Data Modeling Develop and maintain client-specific standard, custom, and master tables and reporting views within Databricks based on a medallion architecture. Assist with transforming and standardizing data from multiple sources into reporting-ready structures. Solve problems and help build solutions related to the data model to meet evolving reporting and analysis needs. Document business rules, transformation logic, and metric definitions. Support maintenance of reusable reporting datasets and standardized data models. Stakeholder Support Act as the primary point of contact for routine data-related questions. Partner with Client Services, Media, Strategy, and Data teams to align on data outputs and expectations. Work with analysts and measurement leads to understand reporting requirements , translate into technical requirements, and provide database-modeled data for reporting. Communicate data issues, impacts, and resolutions to stakeholders. Assist with troubleshooting data discrepancies impacting reporting deliverables. Reporting Support Support Power BI developers and business analysts with data-related questions. Assist with report validation and troubleshooting. Help verify data displayed in dashboards aligns with source systems and business requirements. Provide support for semantic models and reporting datasets when needed. Qualifications Strong SQL and Python skills, in a Databricks environment preferrable. Experience using ETL tools and data manipulation concepts (Funnel.io, DBT, or similar applications). Comfort partnering with Data Engineering on data sources, schemas, and refresh logic. Deep analytical and problem-solving skills related to data storage and structure for reporting. Experience reviewing data logic, KPI definitions, and QA outputs. Basic BI (Tableau, Power BI) skills including data modeling, dashboard structure, calculated fields, usability, data storytelling. Strong written and verbal communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders. Ability to translate complex business reporting requests into modeled data to support current and future analysis. Preferred / Bonus Pharma, HCP, or healthcare media analytics experience, including experience with media PLD (Physician Level Data). Digital media measurement expertise (media KPIs, attribution concepts, omnichannel analysis). Experience inheriting or stabilizing existing data warehouse schemas. Pay Range: $90,000-$110,000 This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting. Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.  - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

 

Who You Are

 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 

 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

jobs.title: Data Scientist - Credit (Retros)
jobs.jd:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.


ABOUT THE TEAM

We’re part of Plaid’s Data organization, building models and insights that help millions of people better understand and grow their financial lives. We use Plaid’s unique financial data to help lenders make more informed decisions and build better credit experiences.

We partner across data science, engineering, product, and Go-to-Market to turn complex data into practical customer recommendations and scalable solutions. We value technical rigor, creativity, user empathy, and teamwork.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on the Credit team, you’ll apply quantitative analysis and deep credit expertise to help lenders make better use of cash flow insights. You’ll work across customer problems, credit policy, and data products—translating Plaid’s data into recommendations and insights that drive business impact and inform product direction.

Your day-to-day responsibilities may include:

 - Deep-dive into model performance for clients, triage issues, and identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

 - Analyze Plaid’s unique data to identify emerging credit risk signals and build and evaluate credit retrospectives.

 - Create tailored recommendations for clients based on their data and Plaid’s insights.

 - Build and maintain data pipelines, including ETL processes using tools such as dbt.

 - Develop metrics, alerts, and dashboards to monitor production machine learning model performance.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the process of developing hands-on recommendations for incorporating cash flow insights into lending decisions, using best practices for account-level decisioning.

 - Improve customer adoption of Plaid Insights through custom analysis tailored to each customer’s needs.

 - Serve as a subject matter expert on credit insights and credit policy implementation, supporting Data Science, Engineering, and Go-to-Market partners.

 - Apply your expertise in quantitative analysis, data mining, and data visualization to develop models and actionable insights.

 - Identify useful signals that can inform machine learning models.

 - Inform and influence Product and Engineering teams through clear analysis and presentations.



WHAT EXCITES YOU

 - Applying data science and credit expertise to real-world lending decisions.

 - Working with Plaid’s unique financial data to uncover emerging credit risk signals and create useful customer insights.

 - Helping lenders make more informed decisions with cash flow data and account-level recommendations.

 - Partnering across Data Science, Engineering, Product, and Go-to-Market to turn analysis into customer and product impact.

 - Working on high-impact problems that can improve financial access and outcomes.



WHAT EXCITES US

 - 2–5 years of industry experience in a financial services Data Science role.

 - Deep familiarity with SQL and Python.

 - Deep understanding of credit risk and the development of underwriting models.

 - Hands-on credit expertise building and maintaining credit policies for lenders.

 - Knowledge of the lending lifecycle and how to optimize each step, including marketing, acquisition, customer management, and collections or recoveries.

 - Demonstrated ability to make data-driven decisions.

 - Nice to have: Experience building data pipelines and automating ETL processes with dbt or similar tools.

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

About the Team

Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.

About the Role

In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.

A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.

 - Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.

 - Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.

 - Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.

 - Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.

 - Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.

Qualifications

 - Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.

 - Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.

jobs.title: AI Research Resident (Algorithms Codesign)
jobs.jd:
NORMAL COMPUTING | BUILD WITH US

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.


THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM

The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication.

Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes.


THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

You'll work on this as a co-design problem. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, so your findings feed architectural decisions rather than implementing against a fixed specification. You'll validate ideas against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.


YOUR NORMAL EXPERIENCE

This is a hands-on research residency: you'll take ownership of a real technical problem in inference algorithms for in-memory compute, work alongside the researchers and engineers building our platform, and be expected to contribute ideas, not just execute someone else's. Your job is to help turn research into production-quality research code that a team can build on. Outside-of-the-box thinking is encouraged.

You'll get direct exposure to the pace, ambiguity, and speed of decision-making that comes with working at a fast-moving, well-funded startup, where the distance between an idea on a whiteboard and a result on real hardware is measured in weeks, not years.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop inference algorithms for in-memory hardware. Understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution and develop algorithms that exploit it natively, demonstrated first in simulation and then on hardware.

Design numerical methods that fit the physics. Design methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.

Build evaluation suites and benchmarks. Help build the evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize how algorithms behave on real hardware and in simulation, and tell us honestly whether any of it actually works.

Translate workloads into hardware constraints. Turn insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for the hardware and architecture teams.

Prototype and iterate rapidly. Move with the hardware as it evolves from simulation to FPGA to silicon.

Drive a research question of your own. Partner with researchers and engineers to scope, run, and iterate on an original technical investigation, with rigorous experimental analysis and documentation along the way.

Co-author a paper. Work with the team to write up your findings for submission to a relevant venue, with mentorship on framing, experiments, and technical writing. One of the two milestones every resident builds toward.

Present at the residency colloquium. Share your work and thinking with the broader Normal Computing research community at the program's capstone event, and get real-time feedback from people building this technology every day.


WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU A GREAT FIT

Currently pursuing or recently completed a graduate degree (MS or PhD, or equivalent research experience) in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field. Publications are a strong plus, but not required at the resident level; a solid research track record is what matters.

A working understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints. Deep production experience isn't expected at the resident level, but the intuition should feel familiar.

Some exposure to inference optimization (quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention), or to stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation.

Strong Python skills, plus some experience with a systems language (C++, Rust, or similar) or with implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks.

Some experience (course projects, research, or otherwise) turning a research idea into working, reasonably reproducible code. You care about whether results replicate, not just whether a demo works once.

Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently.

Bonus: exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures; publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing; or experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined.

Strong written and verbal communication skills; prior experience writing up research (papers, theses, technical reports) is a plus, as is any experience presenting technical work to a live audience.

A bias toward ownership and self-direction. You're energized, not overwhelmed, by the ambiguity and speed of a small, fast-moving startup.

jobs.title: Real Estate Market Intelligence Analyst
jobs.jd:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Neko is opening clinics at pace: from a handful of US sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens and a portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. We are looking for a flexible, quantitative analyst to build the market intelligence behind that growth, using GIS, data, and analytics to decide where we open next, why, and how many clinics a market can support. The work runs from market sizing and member analytics through to site, market, and portfolio performance.

This is a build role. Neko is appointment-based, not footfall-driven, so the standard retail playbook does not transfer, and working out what predicts a successful clinic is the core problem. There is no framework to inherit: you will build the models and processes from scratch, and what you build in year one is what the whole portfolio runs on.

You will report to the Head of US Real Estate and work closely with the Transaction Managers, the Real Estate Associates, and our data analytics and engineering teams, in a small team where you help set the standard.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6-12 MONTHS

 - Market sizing: size the addressable member base by market and trade area, and translate it into how many clinics a market can support and in what order we should enter. This is the first priority of the role.

 - Site selection support: give Real Estate the analysis to justify new markets and infill locations, and to decide clinic sizing and spacing, including overlap and cannibalization as density increases.

 - Member data foundation: work with the internal data analytics and engineering teams to set up the full chain, from data collection to aggregation to analysis. Define our ideal member profile, find where those members live and work, and keep refining it as first-party data accumulates.

 - GIS platform, tool agnostic: use GrowthFactor today and own the catchment definitions, data layers, and scoring logic. Document the logic independently of the tool so it moves with us, and help evaluate and onboard the next platform when the time comes. Make the tool usable by Transaction Managers, not only by you.

 - Scoring and forecasting models: maintain a repeatable, defensible site scoring model and demand forecasts built to be re-run. A reforecast after a slipped opening or a shifted plan should be a scenario switch, not a rebuild.

 - Portfolio, market, and site performance: as clinics open, track and review performance at the portfolio, market, and site level. Compare forecast to actual, separate a bad site from a bad market from a bad launch, surface underperformers early, and document what each opening teaches us. Turn those learnings into updated site selection criteria, scoring weights, and sizing and spacing rules, so every new clinic is chosen with better information than the last.

 - Approval memos and cross-functional support: help produce LOI and Lease Approval Memos by coordinating inputs from Real Estate, Design, Construction, and Legal into a clear, one-page recommendation that leadership can decide from.

 - Process design and redesign: own the evaluation processes the team runs on, and version them. Retire what stops working, rebuild what needs it, and write it down so others can run it without you.

 - AI across the Real Estate team: use Claude and custom agents to eliminate your own manual work, then go further. Identify where AI can save broader team time (market research, data pulls, memo drafting, lease and LOI summaries, pipeline reporting), build reusable prompts, skills, and agents, train teammates to use them, and track the time saved. Be honest about where AI output needs human review.

 - Market packs and benchmarks: produce market entry recommendations, ranked pipeline views, and site-level briefs, backed by per-site cost and occupancy benchmarks by market so deal comparison sits on real data.
   
   


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 6 years in real estate market analytics, site selection, location intelligence, data science, or strategy, ideally supporting multi-site physical expansion.

 - Hands-on GIS experience with GrowthFactor, Esri ArcGIS, Kalibrate, Buxton, SiteZeus, Placer, or similar. We care more that you understand catchment and scoring logic than that you know any one tool, because the tool will change.

 - Strong market sizing and quantitative skills: penetration and capture modeling, regression or other predictive approaches, and scenario and sensitivity analysis. Excel to a high standard.

jobs.title: Market Analyst
jobs.jd:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns a fleet of distributed batteries and the households we serve into a power business that makes money. As a Market Analyst, you’ll know how much Base is earning, where it could lose money, and how it will make money in the next market.

You’ll own P&L (profit and loss) reporting and risk tracking across our battery fleet and retail operations. You’ll build the pricing models behind what we charge members, recommend hedges, and work with Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy to figure out how Base makes money in each new market. Base already does this in ERCOT. Your first job is to do it in PJM.

This role suits someone with a few years of experience in power markets, retail energy, or a related analytical field. You’ll own real decisions early.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build a bottoms-up retail pricing model for PJM that builds upon our ERCOT model.

 - Bring PJM into our risk system and P&L reporting, so we know the margin we earn and how to buy supply.

 - Identify new market opportunities and work closely with stakeholders from Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy teams to bring them to reality.

 - Recommend changes to Base’s hedging strategy in ERCOT and PJM, and track our exposure against risk limits.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets knowledge: you understand wholesale market basics in ERCOT and PJM, including how power is bought, hedged and settled. You know how retail pricing and operations work.

 - Commercial sense: you understand how a retail offer makes or loses money. You can explain the cost to supply it, the margin on it, and the risk in between.

 - Risk and statistics: you think in distributions, not point forecasts. You know power prices are tail heavy. Basic statistics is enough.

 - Coding and SQL: you build reports and models in Python (or another language), pull your own data with SQL, and work through a problem independently.

Nice to have: experience at a retail energy provider, utility supply desk, or trading middle office.



ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight - a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.
